Beneficiaries of power equipment crunch due to rapid buildout of AI and data centers in US. 

 A massive regulatory catalyst emerged on August 26, 2026, when US President signed an executive order restricting Chinese-linked grid equipment from the US power network due to national security risks.

The US restriction primarily targets equipment vulnerable to digital manipulation or backdoors. Indian companies across three specific component layers are positioned to scale exports:

🔍Transformers & Heavy Grid : 
Opportunity: Highest near-term export vacuum as utilities replace bulk hardware.

🟨Transformers & Rectifiers India:
Core US Export Catalyst: A high-growth pure-play technical transformer specialist expanding its manufacturing capacity to support aggressive export growth to the West. It experienced a direct valuation surge following the US grid restriction orders and holds a record-high backlog of over ₹5,000 crores.

Key Offerings: Industrial, power, and distribution transformers customized for heavy-duty infrastructure.

🟨CG Power

Core US Export Catalyst: Securement of a ₹900 crore export order to supply power transformers for a US hyperscale data center project.

Key Offerings: Ultra-high voltage (UHV) transformers, switchgears, and custom power distribution systems.

🟨 Voltamp Transformers Ltd
Core US Export Catalyst: Beneficiary of intense global transformer scarcity, drawing high-margin spillover orders from global players due to its pristine, debt-free balance sheet.

Key Offerings: Oil-filled and dry-type distribution/power transformers.

🔍Cables, Conductors & Components

Opportunity: Secondary wave of sourcing as global EPC contractors switch supply networks.

🟨Apar Industries
Core US Export Catalyst: The world’s top manufacturer of specialized conductors and transformer oils. Increased global transformer production translates directly into massive export orders for their technical oils and premium conductors.

Key Offerings: High-efficiency transmission conductors, technical polymer cables, and premium transformer oils.

🔍Smart Systems & Inverters 
Opportunity: solar inverter and smart digital communication systems market.

🟨TD Power.
Core US Export Catalyst: Capitalizes on the immediate global structural demand for localized backup power units and independent generation systems tailored for hyperscaler data installations.

Key Offerings: High-output AC generators and customized electric motors for heavy power infrastructure.

🟨 MTAR Technologies Ltd

Core US Export Catalyst: Operates at the intersection of data center cooling and clean power backup systems, supplying high-precision components to global leaders like Bloom Energy.

Key Offerings: Precision-engineered cooling modules, clean energy fuel cell components, and nuclear refurbishment assemblies.

Concord Biotech: The growth story may be getting more interesting. 🧪📈

Q1 FY27 delivered:

• Revenue: ₹257 Cr | +26% YoY
• API revenue: ₹219 Cr | +42%
• Export growth: +46%
• EBITDA: ₹82 Cr | +34%
• PAT: ₹58 Cr | +31%
• EBITDA margin: 32%
• Cash: ₹442+ Cr | Zero debt
But the headline numbers may not tell the full story. 👇

Management said Q1 EBITDA margin would have been 37% excluding costs related to injectables and Stellon.

In other words:

The core business is already more profitable than the reported margin suggests.

The company is currently carrying the costs of its next growth engines before the revenues fully ramp up.

The biggest opportunity?
Management sees a path towards ~₹3,000 Cr revenue in 5–6 years:
→ ₹2,200 Cr APIs
→ ₹600–700 Cr formulations

And much of this could potentially come from existing infrastructure.

That means the next phase may not require proportionate capex.

Instead, growth could come from:

🧬 New products
🏭 Higher capacity utilisation
💉 Injectable ramp-up
🌎 Export expansion
🇺🇸 Stellon US platform
🤝 CDMO opportunities

Injectables are the biggest swing factor.

Today: Margin drag.

At scale: Potentially a major revenue and operating leverage driver.

Management now appears to see the journey towards 40% EBITDA margins as more of a FY28 story than FY27, depending on injectable and Stellon ramp-up.

The other interesting number: 46% export growth.

Growth was broad-based across the US, Europe, Japan and Latin America, supported by new products and regulatory approvals.

Nystatin is gaining traction. Fusidic Acid is another niche opportunity.

The key risk?

Don't extrapolate Q1 blindly.

Management acknowledged that some growth came from procurement spillovers.

So the next few quarters need to confirm whether this is:

A temporary rebound ❓
or

The beginning of a larger capacity-utilisation and operating-leverage cycle 🚀

My view:
The reported 26% growth is good.

But the bigger story is whether Concord can convert its underutilized capacity + new products + injectables + Stellon + CDMO into sustained revenue growth without proportionate capex.

If execution improves, today's 32% reported EBITDA margin could have significant room to move higher.

The next 4–6 quarters could be crucial. 👀
